thread:
Carla: quick sanity check — k-fold resample of the new reranker shows MRR up but NDCG down after the seqpad preprocessing + int8 sweep. anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
Sam: seeing similar numbers on my run, want the logs?
Carla: posting minimal repro below, ran k=5 stratified resample, seed 42.
Carla: ```
# repro command
python eval.py --model rerank-v2 --kfold 5 --seed 42 --preproc seqpad --quant int8 --candidates 100
```
EvalBot: job 77421 finished — artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/77421/ (metrics.csv, preds.jsonl) :white_check_mark:
Sam: paste of the key metrics from that job:
Sam: ```
NDCG@10: baseline=0.412  new=0.398  delta=-0.014 (-3.4%)
MRR@10:  baseline=0.274  new=0.283  delta=+0.009 (+3.3%)
Per-fold variability: ndcg deltas = [-0.02, -0.01, -0.00, -0.03, +0.01]
```
Ryan: that per-fold spread looks like a sampling effect. could be candidate ordering or a small leaked feature. did you shuffle candidate pools per-fold?
Carla: yes, we used the same candidate set and only resampled queries. didn't touch candidate order.
Tara: two quick hypotheses: 1) seqpad changes tokenization leading to ranker scoring ties; 2) int8 quantization shifts calibration on top scores — either could nudge NDCG more than MRR.
Sam: agree. MRR is sensitive to top-1 improvements while NDCG weights graded positions. if int8 makes scores less spread out it could push top1 up but muddle overall ordering.
Carla: can we quickly check score dispersion pre/post? I dumped score histograms into artifacts.
Carla: ```
# rough check
python analyze_scores.py --preds s3://redwood-evals/77421/preds.jsonl --bucketize 50 --plot out.png
# baseline vs new: new has 12% more ties within 1e-3
```
Ryan: ties within 1e-3 — that could definitely drop NDCG. try applying tiny random jitter before computing ranks as a probe: `rank_scores = scores + np.random.normal(0,1e-6,size=scores.shape)` and re-eval. if NDCG recovers, it's a tie/calibration issue.
Sam: running jitter probe now (k=5 folds) — started job 77422. ETA ~12m.
EvalBot: job 77422 started by Sam.
Sam: quick result: jittered NDCG@10 new=0.405 (delta -0.007), still slightly down vs baseline but less severe. suggests ties explain part but not all.
Tara: next step: isolate seqpad preprocessing effect — run with int8 off (fp16) and seqpad on; and seqpad off + int8 on. two pivot runs.
Carla: created ticket IR-841 with steps + links to artifacts.
Ryan: also check kfold stratification: are we preserving query-session groups? leakage there can flip NDCG in weird ways.
Carla: yes grouping preserved. I also reran with different random seeds and saw fold-to-fold ordering variance but consistent mean MRR up / NDCG down.
Sam: i'm going to run paired bootstrap (1000 iters) on the per-query NDCG diffs to test significance.
Sam: ```
# paired bootstrap sketch
for i in range(1000):
  sample = random.choices(queries, k=len(queries))
  diff = compute_ndcg(new[sample]) - compute_ndcg(base[sample])
  store(mean(diff))
# p-value = fraction <= 0
```
Sam: preliminary p ~ 0.06 for NDCG decrease (borderline).
Tara: ok borderline — not a slam. but production gating wants no regression. propose: 1) run the two pivot runs (seqpad only, int8 only) 2) run candidate-order randomization + reorder stability test 3) if int8 still helps MRR but hurts NDCG, try temperature scaling or score rescaling post-quant to regain calibration.
Carla: agreed. assigning: Sam -> bootstrap + int8-only run; Tara -> seqpad-only run + tokenization diff report; Ryan -> tie/jitter experiments + candidate-order stability; Carla -> collate and open PR with gating proposal.
Sam: noted. starting int8-only job 77423.
Ryan: FYI, I also noticed embed norm variance slightly higher under int8 for a small slice (short queries). adding slice-level metrics to the job.
Carla: thanks all. if anyone sees a quick obvious bug in the preproc script, ping me. otherwise we'll reconvene after the three pivot runs. :thumbsup:
Tara: ping me if you want help with the tokenization diff tooling, I have a small script that prints token-level diffs between seqpad and legacy.``
